name: The Architect's Workshop
subject: Prompt Engineering
description: Enter a workshop where language is the only building material. Every prompt is a blueprint — imprecise blueprints produce unstable structures. You'll learn to write prompts that reliably produce correct outputs from AI systems, debug failures by reading between the lines of model behavior, and build multi-step agent workflows that don't collapse under complexity.

companions.name: Pascal
companions.personality: Demanding master architect who has built thousands of prompts and has zero tolerance for vague instructions. Believes precision is respect — if you can't say exactly what you mean, you don't know what you mean yet.
companions.speech_pattern: Direct, surgical, cuts to the flaw immediately. Says 'Show me the prompt' before discussing theory. Uses concrete before/after examples. Never praises effort — only praises results. Occasionally reveals a devastating one-line prompt that outperforms a page of instructions.

domains.name: Foundations
concepts: Role, context, and task — the three pillars of every prompt
Output format specification (JSON, markdown, structured text)
Few-shot examples — when they help, when they hurt, how many
System prompts vs user prompts — what goes where and why
Temperature, top-p, and sampling — when to use what
Token economics — prompt length vs output quality trade-offs
domains.mastery_signal: Can take a vague request and rewrite it into a prompt that produces the correct output on the first try, explaining each structural choice

domains.name: Precision & Constraint
concepts: Negative constraints — telling the model what NOT to do
Output guards — preventing hallucination, off-topic drift, and format violations
Delimiter strategies — XML tags, markdown headers, separator lines
Ambiguity detection — finding and eliminating multiple valid interpretations
Instruction hierarchy — what the model prioritizes when instructions conflict
Prompt injection defense — adversarial inputs and how to guard against them
domains.mastery_signal: Can identify every ambiguity in a prompt, predict how the model will misinterpret it, and rewrite it so there's only one valid interpretation

domains.name: Reasoning Control
concepts: Chain-of-thought prompting — when to force reasoning, when to suppress it
Step-by-step decomposition for complex tasks
Self-verification — making the model check its own work
Thinking budgets — controlling how much reasoning the model does
Reasoning vs retrieval — knowing which approach fits the task
Extended thinking and scratchpad patterns
domains.mastery_signal: Can design a prompt that makes the model reason through a multi-step problem correctly, show its work, and catch its own errors before outputting a final answer

domains.name: Multi-Step & Agentic
concepts: Tool use prompting — defining tools, parsing tool calls, handling results
Multi-turn conversation design — maintaining context across exchanges
Agent loops — plan/act/observe cycles with termination conditions
Orchestration patterns — routing between specialized prompts
Error recovery — what to do when a step fails mid-workflow
Context window management — what to keep, what to summarize, what to drop
Prompt chaining — output of one prompt as input to the next
domains.mastery_signal: Can design a multi-step agent workflow with tool use, error handling, and context management that completes a real task without human intervention

domains.name: Evaluation & Debugging
concepts: Prompt debugging — reading model failures to find the prompt flaw
A/B testing prompts — systematic comparison methodology
Evaluation criteria — defining what 'correct' means for subjective tasks
Model-as-judge patterns — using one model to evaluate another
Regression detection — knowing when a prompt change broke something
Cost-quality trade-offs — when a cheaper model with a better prompt beats an expensive model
domains.mastery_signal: Can diagnose why a prompt is failing from the model's output alone, fix it, and verify the fix doesn't break other cases — without trial and error

real_world_application: Write prompts that reliably produce correct outputs from AI systems
